title: JSFL: timeline.currentFrame is read-only — setter missing
description:
Flash 8 JSFL allows `tl.currentFrame = 5` to navigate the timeline to a specific frame. In packages/authoring-ui/src/jsfl/runtime.ts the JsflTimeline interface (line 611) declares `readonly currentFrame: number` and the proxy at line 719 only has a getter (`get currentFrame()`). There is no setter. Any JSFL script that writes `fl.getDocumentDOM().getTimeline().currentFrame = n` silently fails (assignment to a read-only property in strict mode throws; in sloppy mode it is a no-op).

Fix: (1) Remove the `readonly` modifier from `currentFrame` in the JsflTimeline interface. (2) Add a `set currentFrame(n)` in the timeline proxy that updates `state.frameIndex` to the clamped value (0 ≤ n < frameCount) and calls the appropriate setState callback to refresh the UI. Compare with `set currentLayer` (line 716) which correctly updates `state.currentLayerIndex`.

Acceptance: a JSFL script `var tl = fl.getDocumentDOM().getTimeline(); tl.currentFrame = 2;` advances the playhead to frame 2; reading `tl.currentFrame` then returns 2.
